title: Bullish issuer-token coalition expands to 12 firms with DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate
description: Bullish and Equiniti added four trading and tokenization specialists to their issuer-token standards group on November 17, bringing membership to 12 while liquidity and cross-platform trading remain work in progress.
why_it_matters: Tokenized equities need more than blockchain issuance: brokers, transfer agents and liquidity providers must agree on ownership records and secondary-market processes. This coalition includes firms with distinct market-infrastructure roles, but participation is non-binding and does not itself establish a functioning trading venue.
keyTakeaways: DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate joined the Bullish–Equiniti coalition, bringing it to 12 members.
The working group plans to address liquidity mechanics, technical standards and market infrastructure for issuer tokens.
Coalition membership is non-binding and does not require token issuance, trading or liquidity commitments.
body:
Bullish and transfer agent Equiniti announced on November 17 that DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate had joined their Issuer Token Coalition. The four additions increased the working group to 12 members less than two months after its formation. The companies bring different capabilities, spanning institutional execution, market making, consumer finance and blockchain securities infrastructure.

The coalition is developing common approaches to issuer-sponsored tokenized shares. Its next work streams include liquidity arrangements, technical architecture and the commercial systems needed to connect issuers with investors and secondary markets. Bullish said the group had discussed issuer priorities at a New York Stock Exchange gathering on October 27.

The announcement is not a launch of an interoperable stock-trading network. Bullish explicitly describes membership as non-binding: joining does not oblige a firm to issue securities, provide liquidity or list products. Separately, Bullish's planned acquisition of Equiniti is expected to close in January 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. The initiative therefore signals coordination around standards, rather than proof that tokenized shares can already trade freely across platforms.
